experiments.title: Learner-calibrated Sliding Window trajectory
experiments.summary: Manual learner-driven calibration produced the strongest known decomposition/control reference and is preserved as raw evidence plus partial reviewed golden fixtures.

experiments.title: Deterministic learning control and prerequisite remediation
experiments.summary: Deterministic control remains the authority boundary for progression and evidence. Dogfood showed that deterministic structure alone does not guarantee good learner-facing decomposition or representation, so it is retained rather than classified as a failed tutoring method.

experiments.title: Fixed-turn prompt-led model tutoring
experiments.summary: Prompt/model-generated tutoring could satisfy structural checks while learner-visible teaching remained semantically wrong, repetitive, or stuck. Fixed 15-turn completion was invalidated as a success criterion.

experiments.title: Generic TeachingPlan plus prompt, schema, and deterministic validation
experiments.summary: The generic architecture generalized operationally across the public corpus, but manual review exposed coarse generated plans and false-positive acceptance; structural validity did not establish learner-facing quality or completion.

experiments.title: Completion-driven decomposer and reliability qualification
experiments.summary: Current PR #77 direction: fine-grained algorithm/learning graphs, completion-driven tutoring, rotating public evaluation, and hidden promotion. Not yet treated as proven learner-facing calibration.

experiments.title: Sol calibration-artifact transfer to Two Sum
experiments.summary: Distill the successful Sliding Window calibration into a durable artifact, then give only that artifact plus Two Sum to a fresh Sol teacher session and a frozen synthetic student. Review the complete rendered HTML interaction turn by turn before any Luna distillation work.
